newsitem.title: INDONESIA: OPINION - It's still time for bargain hunting.
newsitem.headline: OPINION - It's still time for bargain hunting.

text.p: By Felix D'Souza, head of research
PT Peregrine Sewu Securities
JAKARTA, Feb 13 - A low market valuation of just 15.7 x 1997 earnings and earnings growth of close to 20 percent pa expected through 1998 are enticing, despite a strong three-month performance.
As elections approach in a relatively calm political atmosphere, the significant discount applied to the market following the July 1996 riots is starting to shrink.

We believe the political risk premium is still too high and is based on perceived risks rather than actual risks. The market should recognise the clear distinction between uncertain politics and what is a very stable economy.

Following in the wake of Asian and European investors, U.S. money is at last starting to shift from disappointing markets such as South Korea and Thailand into Indonesia. Most U.S. investors are still underweight in Indonesia but there is strong momentum behind the move to overweight, which will provide strong demand for stock in 1997.
IMPROVED LIQUIDITY AND MORE INVESTABLE STOCKS
On top of relatively cheap valuations, improving market liquidity will be a major spur behind multiple expansion.

Over the course of last year, average daily trading volume almost doubled on the back of a sharp jump in local market participation. Local investors represented just 35 percent of daily trading volume at the start of 1996, but took up 55 percent of daily trading by December.
Foreign trading volumes remained surprisingly steady throughout the year and the increase in the proportion of domestic volume is directly attributable to increased local trading.

We predict very strong growth in local trading volumes will continue in 1997 and 1998, providing better market and liquidity and broadening the rangs of stocks that meet the liquidity requirements for international investors.

The local trading is driven by wealthy retail clients with better access to margin trading, brokerage branches and stock exchange information and by a newly emerging local institutional investor base driven by high savings rates, financial deregulation and lower interest deposit rates.

At this stage in the market's development, the nature of the local investor base is different to that in Thailand or Taiwan. Although more speculative than foreign investors, the Indonesian local investors are not idle housewives punting with the week's shopping allowance. The local money tends to stay in the market and is often invested comparatively scientifically.
760 IS EASY AND 800 COULD BE BREACHED
Based on 20 percent earnings growth, we believe the JKSE should easily cross 760 by year-end (from 632 at the close of 1996).

On a 12-month view, a JKSE index level of 800 should be achievable given the shrinking perceived political risk, positive economic outlook, increased foreign weightings, falling local interest rates and dramatic improvement in stock liquidity.
STRATEGY SHOULD CENTRE AROUND DOMESTIC PLAYS
Sectors most likely to perform in 1997 are all related to a domestic consumption. Although slowing from an above-trend base, GDP growth will remain at a healthy 7.4 percent in 1997.
Inflation shows signs of slowing and should remain manageable, allowing the central bank to slightly ease its tight monetary stance.
Interest rates will continue to fall in a controlled manner, with deposit rates set to come down another 100 b.p. in the first half of the year and lending rates to follow suit in the second half.

The lure of those overquoted Indonesian themes -- 200 million consumers, a rapidly growing middle class and abundant natural resources -- is particularly strong in 1997 and should provide the means to significant market performance.

By contrast, the export sector is still plagued by poor productivity, weak regional markets, poor prices and a rupiah likely to remain stubbornly stronger than expectations (although benign inflation helps to control the real effective exchange rate against many Asian trading partners).
STOCK SELECTION HIGHLIGHTS
In line with our view on the benefits of holding domestic consumption this year, we advise investors to overweight banks, cigarettes, niche property plays and transport plays.

OVERWEIGHT BANKS - Share prices for large liquid banks should benefit from the continued liquidity driven rally. Fundamentals look attractive on the back of 20 percent loan growth, stable margins and higher fee income following recent industry deregulation. Lippo Bank and BDNI are our top picks in the sector on efficiency gains and a high proportion of low-cost retail funding.

OVERWEIGHT CIGARETTES - Three-year compound earnings growth and returns on equity in excess of 25 percent justify the rich premium for the sector over the market. Gudang Garam is one of the best-managed companies in Indonesia, and should post strong earnings growth despite slight losses in market share as it concentrates on profitability over the next couple of years.

OVERWEIGHT PROPERTY - Enormous, undervalued land banks provide the impetus for earnings growth in the property sector and result in large discounts to NAV. Falling interest rates will trigger interest in the sector after a three-year sector stock price underperformance.
However, the expected fall in rates during 1997 will be inadequate to spark a true property boom, particularly in the oversupplied landed residential segment.

Our key picks are niche players deriving growth from non-investment led demand. Industrial property specialists and Jaya Real Property, a niche player in the low-cost residential segment, are likely to perform strongly.
Commercial property developer, Mulia Land, should also do well as the Mulia group continues to inject quality earnings-generated assets into the listed vehicle at large discounts NAV.

OVERWEIGHT RETAIL - Corporate strategy is improving in the retail sector as companies concentrate on more-lucrative target markets, avoid over-expansion, and improve store efficiency and inventory control.

Ramayana Lestari Sentosa, which will post strong growth based on its appeal to the working classes, continues to shine, but Matahari Putra Prima also looks attractive now that the Lippo group has announced the closure of six unprofitable stores and improvements in cash managament.

OVERWEIGHT LAND TRANSPORTATION - Given a rising population in Jakarta and a growing group of commuters from satellite cities, we expect strong earnings for bus and taxi operator Steady Safe and tollroad operator Citra Marga Nusaphala Persada.
